rulings.challenge_claim: The frame-ownership call at 36:4 is right, but the row's adonai argument is false in the bytes - the courtly token it quotes is not the same form as the divine title - and it leaves the identical courtly token inside its own span and the YHWH-speech attribution at its own closing verse unengaged.
rulings.grounds: Object re-derived before the digit. Swept object: the whitespace-delimited, unprefixed and unsuffixed adonai token, finals-normalized, book-wide. From bytes: 47 verses carry one, and no verse carries two (the per-pointed-form verse counts sum to exactly 47). Of those, 44 verses are qamats-pointed under the nun - the divine title, e.g. אֲדֹנָ֛י (oshb:Isa.6.1, byte) - and EXACTLY 3 are hiriq-pointed: MT 36:8, 36:9, 36:12, all three inside this cluster. The challenge's digits reproduce exactly and its count-object is the right one; the book's wider prefix-tolerant bare-adonai census of 51 verses is a different object and does not conflict. The row's own quoted token is אֲדֹנִ֖י (oshb:Isa.36.8, byte), hiriq-pointed. Same consonantal skeleton as the divine title, different pointed form - so boundary_rationale's 'the same bare-adonai form that elsewhere in the book addresses the divine Adonai' is FALSE at byte tier and true only at skeleton tier, and it stands two clauses after an explicit 'tier: byte' label with no tier named for the identity. The tier-disclosure standard bites: a skeleton-tier identity satisfies the byte-grounded bar only with the tier honestly named. The courtly/divine split here is visible in the POINTING, not merely in the referent - that is a genuine find. WHERE THE CHALLENGE OVER-FRAMES (the refinement): the row's adonai argument is not uniformly false. device_notes already states the identity correctly as a CONSONANTAL one - 'the same consonants carry elsewhere in the book' - and names the role split rather than assuming it; the courtly referent is byte-supported by the appositional 'the king of Assyria' in the same clause. The defect is confined to one word ('form') in boundary_rationale plus the missing tier label: a one-clause repair, not a rebuilt argument. Corrected finding: a tier-mislabel in one field beside a correct statement in another, i.e. an internal inconsistency, not a false argument. The challenge's two remaining items are byte-confirmed and are the heavier half of it. (a) The identical hiriq-pointed token recurs INSIDE the row's own span at עַבְדֵ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י (oshb:Isa.36.9, byte) and is undisclosed - a symmetry miss on the object the row itself elected to engage, and symmetry is a sweep, not a spot fix. (b) The row's own closing verse reads יְהוָה֙ אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Isa.36.10, byte) - a YHWH-speech attribution placed in the Assyrian herald's mouth at the row's terminus - and MT 36:10 is absent from the book's amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency census (52 verses); a row whose entire case is frame ownership owes that verse a word. One correction to the challenge's parenthesis: that census reaches further into this narrative zone than it lists (MT 37:6, 37:21, 37:33, 38:1, 38:5, 39:6), but MT 36:10 is outside it either way, so the point stands.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'the same bare-adonai form that elsewhere in the book addresses the divine Adonai' with a consonantal-identity statement carrying its tier explicitly (same consonantal skeleton, skeleton tier; the pointing differs - hiriq here against the qamats of the divine title), matching what device_notes already says. boundary_rationale or device_notes: add the in-span recurrence at oshb:Isa.36.9 as a spliced pointed run with its tier, completing symmetry on the adonai object across the whole span rather than at one site. boundary_rationale: engage oshb:Isa.36.10, the row's own closing verse, naming the YHWH-speech attribution inside the herald's speech and stating that it is not a member of the amar-plus-YHWH adjacency census (52 verses). observed_substrate_signals: no driver moves here, so the dependent-field cascade does not open. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the finals-normalized bare-adonai sweep that killed the original - the token at oshb:Isa.36.8 must come back hiriq-pointed against the 44 qamats-pointed divine-title verses, the identity claim must carry its tier, and EVERY hiriq site inside the row's own span (oshb:Isa.36.8 AND oshb:Isa.36.9) must be disclosed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The language handling and the doubled ketiv/qere disclosure are correct, but the row's claim that the verse repeats the courtly bare-adonai form twice over is false in the bytes: its two adonai tokens are two different forms and only one belongs to the bare-token object.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from the verse bytes. MT 36:12 carries two adonai-family tokens: אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ and אֲדֹנִ֔י (oshb:Isa.36.12, byte). They differ at BYTE tier and also at finals-normalized SKELETON tier (a final kaf on the first, absent from the second), and only the second is a member of the bare-token object, which stands hiriq-pointed at exactly 3 verses book-wide (MT 36:8, 36:9, 36:12). So 'The same verse repeats the courtly bare-adonai form, twice over' fails twice over: not the same form, and the first token is outside the bare census entirely. It doubles a count-object inside the book's largest ketiv/qere class. What survives, and the remedy must preserve it: the REFERENTIAL half of the row's sentence is right - both tokens name a human master relation, neither the divine title - so the cure is the form/count wording, not the role claim. The challenge's zone enumeration also reproduces exactly from bytes: four distinct adonai-family forms across MT 36:8 and 36:9 (אֲדֹנִ֖י), MT 36:12 (אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ), MT 37:4 (אֲדֹנָיו֙) and MT 37:6 (אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֑ם), all byte tier. Verified in the row's favour and NOT defects: MT 36:12 carries 2 ketiv/qere notes, one of the book's four doubled-note verses, and the row discloses it as single-witness apparatus without arguing it as boundary evidence; the herald's title is genuinely two tokens, רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה (oshb:Isa.36.12, byte), so a single-token needle finds nothing; and the language handling is correct - the Aramaic request is narrated story content, no Aramaic verse label is asserted, which is the documented false-positive class in this zone. The challenge's ketiv/qere naming point is real but secondary: the row's pointed run stages the two unpointed ketiv forms חראיהם and שיניהם beside their pointed qere partners צוֹאָתָ֗ם and מֵימֵ֥י רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם (oshb:Isa.36.12, byte) under one 'tier: byte' label without naming which is which. The run IS byte-accurate against source, so this is a naming gap inside the campaign's largest K/Q inventory, not a quote defect - it belongs in the remedy, not in the severity.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'The same verse repeats the courtly bare-adonai form, twice over' with the byte-true statement - the verse carries TWO DISTINCT adonai-family forms, a 2ms-suffixed and a 1cs-suffixed token (distinct at byte AND at finals-normalized skeleton tier), of which only the 1cs token is a member of the bare-adonai census (3 hiriq-pointed verses: MT 36:8, 36:9, 36:12) - and KEEP the referential claim, which stands. device_notes: when disclosing the doubled ketiv/qere at oshb:Isa.36.12, name WHICH tokens in the quoted run are ketiv (unpointed) and which are qere (pointed), since the row slices and counts inside that verse. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the finals-normalized adonai-family sweep of MT 36:12 - the two tokens must come back as distinct forms at byte AND skeleton tier, and the bare-token census must still return exactly 3 hiriq-pointed verses with only ONE of MT 36:12's two tokens inside it.

rulings.challenge_claim: Frame ownership and the mid-speech parashah disclosure are exact, but the seam the row actually decides is argued in English only, and its prose substitutes 'Hebrew' for a byte term neither witness renders that way.
rulings.grounds: Verified in the row's favour first: both frames are royal-messenger and correctly owned - כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ (oshb:Isa.36.14, byte) and כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֗וּר (oshb:Isa.36.16, byte) - two of the four royal-messenger sites (MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3) against 44 divine-frame verses, with no divine frame inside the span. The mark claim is exact: MT 36:16 carries a SAMEKH, correctly typed, single-witness, correctly disclosed as falling mid-speech and not read as a break, and it is the ONLY PE or SAMEKH inside MT 36:13-36:20, so span-relevant symmetry is satisfied. Gap 1 confirmed: the row's two pointed splices are MT 36:14 and MT 36:16, both mid-span, while the seam the row actually decides - MT 36:13, the herald standing, calling in a loud voice, naming a language, turning to a new audience - is nowhere spliced. Its bytes are וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְקוֹל גָּד֖וֹל יְהוּדִ֑ית (oshb:Isa.36.13, byte). Gap 2 confirmed, and it is what makes gap 1 bite: boundary_rationale says the proclamation was made 'in Hebrew rather than Aramaic'. The byte term inside that unspliced run is יְהוּדִ֑ית (oshb:Isa.36.13, byte), the Judahite-language noun, which the row's own English quotation renders “in the Jews' language” (web:Isa.36.13). Neither witness reads 'Hebrew' there. In a book whose every verse label is Hebrew, and where the neighbouring Aramaic request is the documented story-content false-positive class, substituting the label-word for the byte term is exactly the conflation the language layer is watched for - and the row's own immediately preceding unit handles that distinction correctly, so this is an internal inconsistency as well. Held against inflating severity: the WEB-quotation mandate IS satisfied at 36:13 (curly-quoted run plus an inline web: ref in the same field), no boundary evidence is fabricated, no Aramaic verse label is asserted, and the frame architecture is untouched. This is an evidence-completeness and gloss-accuracy defect. Low is the right register.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: splice the pointed onset run of oshb:Isa.36.13 with its tier, so the seam the row decides is carried by the bytes rather than by the rendering alone. boundary_rationale: replace 'in Hebrew rather than Aramaic' with the byte term - the Judahite-language noun, spliced and tier-labelled - keeping the contrast with the Aramaic request as narrated story content, never as a verse-language label. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the language-layer check that killed the original - the row must name the byte term at oshb:Isa.36.13 and must not assert 'Hebrew' as the proclamation's named language while every verse of the book keeps its Hebrew language label; and the seam verse must carry a byte-tier pointed splice, not only an English rendering.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the join across the chapter division is byte-supportable, but the row never quotes the catchword that supports it, never engages the one tier-3 mark inside its span that falls exactly at the junction it joins, and leaves a byte-true covering-in-sackcloth tie straddling its own closing seam undisclosed. LF: the row's forward boundary misplaces 37:1 on the officials'-report side of the seam, when the stronger tier-1 signal opens Hezekiah's own extended response there instead.
rulings.grounds: CONVERGENCE: the two challenges land on ONE defect at the row's FORWARD seam, reached from opposite directions, plus two items that belong to OL alone. SAME DEFECT (LF's whole challenge = OL's third item). Bytes: MT 36:22 closes with the delegation as subject, וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.36.22, byte); MT 37:1 opens a fresh wayehi-plus-explicit-subject clause, וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ (oshb:Isa.37.1, byte), shifting the acting subject from the delegation to the king; its וַיִּתְכַּ֣ס בַּשָּׂ֔ק (oshb:Isa.37.1, byte) is picked up immediately at MT 37:2 by מִתְכַּסִּ֖ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֑ים (oshb:Isa.37.2, byte) - the same verbal root in a different stem plus the same noun pluralized, ROOT tier, not byte-identical - while MT 37:2 itself opens וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח (oshb:Isa.37.2, byte) with Hezekiah still the subject. The row's forward bound therefore cuts between two clauses that share both subject and device. LF states the rival (37:1 belongs with Hezekiah's own response arc, continuing into the embassy to Isaiah); OL supplies the byte tie that arms it; both are correct, and the row's strongest_rejected_alternative engages only the REAR edge. One defect, one cure. DISTINCT, OL ONLY (a): the sole PE or SAMEKH inside MT 36:21-37:1 is the SAMEKH at MT 36:22 - keyed to the verse immediately before the row's own INTERNAL join. Tier-3 weak, single-witness, never a driver, and its absence would never be counterevidence; but PRESENCE exactly at the join the row makes turns the row's one disclosed corroborating signal into a weak rival to its own decision, disclosed without its bearing stated. DISTINCT, OL ONLY (b): the join's strongest byte warrant goes unquoted - קְרוּעֵ֣י בְגָדִ֑ים (oshb:Isa.36.22, byte) answered across the junction by וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת בְּגָדָ֑יו (oshb:Isa.37.1, byte): shared root, distinct pointed forms, ROOT tier and not byte-identical recurrence - while the row argues 'the same participants and the same report-and-response movement' in English. The challenge's tier label there is exact. SCOPE, stated so the author wave cannot over-reach: the respan LF's rival implies - carrying 37:1 forward with Hezekiah's response - is a BOUNDARY PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption, and is never author work. Every remedy below is prose and disclosure repair only and leaves the bound exactly as drafted.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: splice the tear-and-garment pair across the internal junction (oshb:Isa.36.22 and oshb:Isa.37.1) with its tier named as ROOT tier, not byte-identical recurrence, replacing the English-only 'same participants and same report-and-response movement' warrant. boundary_rationale or device_notes: state the BEARING of the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.36.22 on the row's own internal join (tier-3, single-witness, weak, never a driver, absence never counterevidence) rather than only its existence. device_notes: disclose the covering-in-sackcloth tie across the row's own CLOSING seam (oshb:Isa.37.1 to oshb:Isa.37.2), root tier, under the cross-seam cohesion rule. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut it to engage the FORWARD rival - that MT 37:1 opens Hezekiah's own response arc continuing into the embassy at MT 37:2 - since the currently disclosed rival argues only the rear edge; one sentence, plus at most a second carrying the rival disclosure. BOUNDARY PROPOSAL (boss adoption required, explicitly NOT author work): respan to close this unit at Isa.36.22 and open the next at Isa.37.1. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the cross-seam cohesion sweep that killed the original - every byte-true or root-true device straddling EITHER of this row's seams (tear/garment at the internal join, cover/sackcloth at the closing seam) must be disclosed with its tier, and the rejected alternative must name the forward rival, not only the rear one.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both frame calls in this row are correct, but its koh-amar digit is wrong: the Assyrian king owns three prior royal-messenger sites, not two, and this cluster's own preceding rows name all three.
rulings.grounds: Census re-derived, object named first. The koh-amar frame census is 48 verses, split 44 divine-frame against exactly 4 royal-messenger verses: MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3. Of those four, the ASSYRIAN KING owns THREE - כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר (oshb:Isa.36.4, byte), כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ (oshb:Isa.36.14, byte), כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֗וּר (oshb:Isa.36.16, byte) - and the fourth is this row's own Judahite-king frame, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ (oshb:Isa.37.3, byte). device_notes' 'the Assyrian king's two prior sites' undercounts by one, and 'both the royal-messenger sites in chapter 36' is wrong on its face: chapter 36 holds THREE. This is the one digit class the narrative zone flags as meaningless unless the frame owner is named - the owner IS named here and the digit is still wrong, so the 'THIRD koh-amar frame-owner' architecture claim rests on a bad census, and it contradicts the row's own preceding units, which between them name all three Assyrian sites. Both ownerships verified correct and untouched: the Judahite king's frame at MT 37:3, and the divine frame כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.37.6, byte), the tier-1 object. This is therefore a digit repair inside a sound frame argument, not a driver swap - observed_substrate_signals, unit_type, confidence and rejected_alternative do not re-open. The challenge's secondary point is verified: MT 37:6 carries the prefixed speech-commission כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן three tokens before the counted frame כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה in the SAME verse (oshb:Isa.37.6, byte), and the row quotes the whole verse without distinguishing them - the exact distinction the following unit's census refusal turns on, with its byte anchor already sitting inside this row.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: correct the digit - the Assyrian king owns THREE prior royal-messenger koh-amar sites (MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16), all three in chapter 36, of the 4-verse royal-messenger set against 44 divine-frame verses; the Judahite king's frame at MT 37:3 is the fourth royal SITE and the second royal frame-OWNER. Re-word the 'third frame-owner' sentence so the owner count and the site count are stated separately and each names its object. device_notes or boundary_rationale: distinguish the prefixed speech-commission from the counted frame inside oshb:Isa.37.6, since the row quotes both in one run. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the frame-ownership census that killed the original - the royal-messenger set must resolve to exactly MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3, with the Assyrian-owned subset at 3, and every digit in the row must name WHOSE frame it counts.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row rightly refuses to inflate the koh-amar census at 37:10, but it mislabels that verse's verb form as an imperative, builds a letter-versus-in-person contrast its own span's bytes do not carry, and makes a recurrence claim with no quoted form and no tier.
rulings.grounds: All three defects re-derived from bytes; one of the challenge's own tiers is corrected UPWARD, and a fourth defect neither primary raised is recorded. (1) FORM CLASS. MT 37:10 opens כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן (oshb:Isa.37.10, byte) - a taw-prefix conjugation, 2mp, with paragogic nun. The book's actual imperative of that verb stands inside this same cluster at אִמְרוּ נָ֖א (oshb:Isa.36.4, byte), and both witnesses part exactly there: “Thus you shall speak to Hezekiah king of Judah” (web:Isa.37.10) against “Now tell Hezekiah” (web:Isa.36.4). device_notes' 'plain imperative-to-speak construction' is contradicted by the letter bytes and by both renderings; with no morphology layer staged, a form-class label the bytes contest should have been held, not asserted. What SURVIVES and must be preserved through the repair: the row's substantive refusal is correct - MT 37:10 is absent from the 48-verse koh-amar census. (2) LETTER-VERSUS-IN-PERSON. The row's own span MT 37:8-13 carries no document noun. A finals-normalized skeleton sweep of that consonantal string over MT 36:1-39:8 returns 5 verses, and the homograph split is what decides the point: MT 36:3 is the scribe title, MT 36:19 and MT 37:13 are the place name סְפַרְוָ֑יִם (oshb:Isa.36.19, byte), and only MT 37:14 and MT 39:1 carry the document noun - so the row's OWN closing verse holds the homograph, not the noun. Inside the span the bytes read וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.37.9, byte): messengers dispatched with a speech commission. The noun first appears ONE VERSE PAST the row's close, plural and taken from those same messengers' hand, הַסְּפָרִ֛ים מִיַּ֥ד הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.37.14, byte), which contradicts the contrast rather than grounding it. The argument works in the English singular, “Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers” (web:Isa.37.14), and not in the Hebrew. (3) UNTIERED RECURRENCE - and STRONGER than the challenge tiered it. The two-token run אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ (oshb:Isa.36.18, byte) recurs BYTE-IDENTICAL at exactly 2 verses book-wide (MT 36:18, MT 37:12; sweep: 2 verses). CORRECTION: the taunt-chain place name סְפַרְוָ֑יִם that the challenge tiered as skeleton is in fact BYTE-identical at exactly those same 2 verses (MT 36:19, MT 37:13; sweep: 2 verses, byte tier). The row asserts the cross-row restatement in prose with no quoted form and no tier while the byte evidence is that strong. NEW FINDING (raised by neither primary): strongest_rejected_alternative rejects a split at MT 37:10 on the stated ground that there is 'no independent frame or addressee marker of its own at that verse'. The bytes refute the ground: MT 37:10 opens כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ (oshb:Isa.37.10, byte) - an explicit speech commission with a NAMED addressee. The bound may well be right, since the commission is embedded inside the narrated sending, but its stated ground is byte-false and must be re-argued rather than repeated.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: strike the form-class label 'plain imperative-to-speak construction' and replace it with what the bytes carry - a prefixed second-person plural form with paragogic nun, byte tier, contrasted with the imperative at oshb:Isa.36.4 - while KEEPING the census refusal, which is correct (MT 37:10 is not among the 48 koh-amar verses). boundary_rationale: strike or re-ground 'sent this time by letter rather than delivered in person'. Inside MT 37:8-13 the bytes carry messengers plus a speech commission and no document noun; if the letter is argued at all it must be cited to oshb:Isa.37.14, outside the span, in the plural, and mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs. boundary_rationale: quote and tier the cross-row restatement - the byte-identical two-token gods-of-the-nations run at oshb:Isa.36.18 and oshb:Isa.37.12 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier) and the byte-identical place name at oshb:Isa.36.19 and oshb:Isa.37.13 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier) - and mirror the out-of-span verses in boundary_evidence_refs. strongest_rejected_alternative (NEW FINDING cure): re-argue the rejection of a split at MT 37:10 without the false ground; the verse DOES carry a named addressee in an explicit speech commission, so the rejection must rest on that commission being embedded inside the narrated sending, not on the absence of an addressee marker. One sentence, plus at most a second carrying the rival disclosure. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the sweeps that killed the original - the document-noun sweep must return no in-span hit for MT 37:8-13 once the place-name homograph is split out; every recurrence claim must carry a quoted pointed run, a named tier and a digit; the form-class label must match the letter bytes; and the rejected alternative must not assert the absence of an addressee marker at MT 37:10.

rulings.challenge_claim: The frame-plus-speech bound is defensible, but the row never splices the prayer frame its whole argument rests on and does not disclose that the following verse binds itself back to this unit's prayer by the same root.
rulings.grounds: Both gaps confirmed from bytes. (1) The row's stated driver is that frame and speech stay together, and the frame verse itself is never spliced: MT 37:15 reads וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ אֶל יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.37.15, byte) - the entire warrant for holding the narrated act together with the prayer's content - and it is argued in English, while the row's two pointed runs sit at MT 37:14 and MT 37:20, the span's outer edges. (2) MT 37:21 carries אֲשֶׁר֙ הִתְפַּלַּ֣לְתָּ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Isa.37.21, byte), naming this unit's prayer as the ground of the answering word on the same verbal root as the unspliced frame verb - ROOT tier, not byte-identical - straddling the row's closing seam and undisclosed. Also verified: no PE or SAMEKH falls inside MT 37:14-37:20 (tier-3 absence, never counterevidence, so no symmetry debt there). The minor gloss points hold: MT 37:14 reads the plural הַסְּפָרִ֛ים with a singular object suffix on the reading verb in the same run (oshb:Isa.37.14, byte) against WEB's “Hezekiah received the letter” (web:Isa.37.14); and its definite הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים resolves the indefinite מַלְאָכִ֔ים of MT 37:9 (byte tier) across the row's opening seam. WHERE THE CHALLENGE OVER-FRAMES (the refinement): item (2)'s DIRECTIONAL FORCE. The challenge concludes that the tie 'argues continuity against the row's assertion of a self-contained rhetorical terminus'. That is not established. The anaphor sits INSIDE a fresh divine koh-amar frame - כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.37.21, byte), one of the 44 divine-frame verses and a tier-1 seam signal - and an anaphoric back-reference under a NEW frame presupposes the prior unit is complete as readily as it argues continuation. Corrected finding: two disclosure and splice gaps, both real and both owed under cross-seam cohesion, with NO evidence against the bound, which stands. Severity low is right and should not rise on a directional reading the bytes do not carry.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: splice the pointed prayer-frame run at oshb:Isa.37.15 with its tier, since the frame-plus-speech driver rests entirely on that verse while the two existing splices sit at the span's outer edges. device_notes: disclose the prayer-verb tie across the row's closing seam (oshb:Isa.37.15 to oshb:Isa.37.21) at ROOT tier, stating that it stands inside a fresh divine koh-amar frame and is therefore consistent with the seam rather than counterevidence to it. boundary_rationale: match the gloss to the bytes - the noun at oshb:Isa.37.14 is plural with a singular object suffix on the reading verb; if 'the letter' is retained it must be marked as the English rendering. rulings.challenge_claim: The span's mandated ketiv/qere disclosure is missing and four byte-true devices inside the span go unengaged, including a second divine speech-frame that licenses an undisclosed internal cut and the row's own closing clause, which recurs verbatim two units later.
rulings.grounds: Every item re-derived and confirmed; one sub-point is corrected for scope. (1) MT 37:30 sits inside the span and carries one ketiv/qere note; the doubled pair stands in the verse bytes as ואכול וְאִכְל֥וּ (oshb:Isa.37.30, byte), the first form unpointed. Undisclosed. The internal asymmetry alleged is real: the Babylonian-embassy row covering MT 39:1-39:4 in this same cluster DOES disclose its own ketiv/qere verse. Span-relevant disclosure symmetry is a sweep, not a spot fix. (2) MT 37:33 opens לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר (oshb:Isa.37.33, byte) - a SECOND divine-owner koh-amar frame inside the span. In MT 36:1-39:8 the divine sites are 37:6, 37:21, 37:33, 38:1, 38:5 against the four royal-messenger sites 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3. The row's rejected alternative addresses only the front edge (MT 37:21). CORRECTION for scope, and it changes the remedy: the ruling that governs this zone keeps the taunt-song inside the frame that introduces it, so MT 37:33 is NOT a live cut candidate. What is owed is disclosure and a rival that engages the strongest INTERNAL signal - not a cut, and no author-side respan. (3) MT 37:34 closes נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.37.34, byte) - the ONLY postpositive oracle signature in MT 36:1-39:8 (sweep: 1 verse in the zone, of 23 book-wide), standing one verse before the row's own close and unengaged. (4) MT 37:23 carries אֶל קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.37.23, byte), the only Holy-One-of-Israel title site in the narrative zone (sweep: 1 of 25 title verses book-wide); MT 37:24 carries חֵרַ֣פְתָּ אֲדֹנָי֒ (oshb:Isa.37.24, byte) - a QAMATS-pointed bare-adonai token, i.e. the DIVINE side of the very role split this same part argues on its courtly side a few units earlier, which makes the omission an internal asymmetry too; and the remnant family stands at MT 37:31 הַנִּשְׁאָרָ֖ה and MT 37:32 שְׁאֵרִ֔ית (byte tier), two of the four objects on that root. None engaged, and observed_substrate_signals carries only two keys for a 15-verse span. (5) The row quotes MT 37:35 in full but does not note that its opening clause וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י עַל הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את (oshb:Isa.37.35, byte) recurs at MT 38:6 as וְגַנּוֹתִ֖י עַל הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּֽאת (oshb:Isa.38.6, byte) - 2 verses book-wide at finals-normalized SKELETON tier, NOT byte tier (the accents differ), which is exactly how the challenge tiered it - reactivated inside the healing narrative two units on and bracketing the row's own rear seam. Verified in the row's favour and untouched: the SAMEKH marks at MT 37:32 and MT 37:35 match the inventory under the correct type, single-witness, never conflated with the zone's one petuchah at MT 39:8; the divine frame at MT 37:21 is correctly owned; the taunt-song is correctly held inside its frame; and the WEB layout statement is accurate and correctly excluded as tier-4. The bound is defensible - the challenge is against the evidence set, and it lands.

NOT a respan: no boundary change is authorised by this remedy. boundary_rationale or device_notes: engage the postpositive oracle signature at oshb:Isa.37.34 (sweep: 1 verse in MT 36:1-39:8, 23 book-wide), standing one verse before the row's own close. device_notes: disclose the in-span device set the row leaves silent - the qadosh-Israel title at oshb:Isa.37.23 (sweep: 1 of 25 title verses), the qamats-pointed bare-adonai token at oshb:Isa.37.24 named on the DIVINE side of the zone's role split, and the two remnant-family objects at oshb:Isa.37.31 and oshb:Isa.37.32 with each object named before any digit. device_notes: disclose the closing-clause reactivation at oshb:Isa.38.6 under cross-seam cohesion, tier-labelled as finals-normalized skeleton tier (sweep: 2 verses), NOT as byte-identical recurrence. observed_substrate_signals: extend to cover the devices newly argued (divine-frame, oracle-signature, divine-title and remnant-family keys) using the dotted signal-key taxonomy only. boundary_evidence_refs: mirror every out-of-span verse newly argued in prose, including oshb:Isa.38.6. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut to engage the strongest INTERNAL rival (the frame onset at MT 37:33) rather than only the front edge; one sentence, plus at most a second carrying the rival disclosure. supported_sample.notes: Re-derived from the verse bytes rather than from the frame census, so the check is independent of the inventory both primaries leaned on. Across MT 37:36, 37:37 and 37:38 there is not a single token of the amar root, no koh token, no neum token and no dabar token, and neither witness carries any quoted speech in the span - the three verses are narration end to end, opening וַיֵּצֵ֣א מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַיַּכֶּה֙ (oshb:Isa.37.36, byte) and וַיְהִי֩ ה֨וּא מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֜ה בֵּ֣ית (oshb:Isa.37.38, byte). Cross-checked against the frame census afterwards for agreement: the zone's koh-amar sites (MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3, 37:6, 37:21, 37:33, 38:1, 38:5) and its sole postpositive signature נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.37.34, byte) all fall OUTSIDE MT 37:36-37:38, and the amar-plus-YHWH adjacency census does not reach into the span either. Byte derivation and census agree. Two further load-bearing disclosures spot-checked and also clean: both marks the row discloses are SAMEKH in the inventory at MT 37:35 (front seam) and MT 37:38 (own close), correctly typed and never conflated with the zone's single petuchah at MT 39:8; and no ketiv/qere note falls inside the span (the zone's notes are at MT 36:12, 37:30 and 39:2). Chs 36-39 are identity numbering, so no dual or numeric qualifier is owed anywhere in this row. No defect found.
